note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: # close other heavy programs first: only the ratios between runs matter, not the exact milliseconds
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-perf, C:\work\01-load-everything.patch -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

screens.name: counters
steps: Tab 2: $id = Get-Content api.pid; dotnet tool run dotnet-counters monitor -p $id --counters System.Runtime   (the live table: allocation rate, GC collections per generation, GC pause time moving while the load runs; press q to stop)
Then: bash scripts/profile.sh http://localhost:5080 $id 15   and keep the final line 'window 14 s: ... allocated ... MB ... GC pause ... gen0/gen1/gen2 ...' (say your own numbers)
screens.note: dotnet-counters monitor is a live console UI and only renders on a real console, so it is not played by the scripted terminal. If it cannot attach on Windows without elevation, run the terminal as the same user as the API.

screens.name: trace
steps: Windows Terminal: show the dotnet-trace collect line inside scripts/profile.sh (profile dotnet-sampled-thread-time, --format Speedscope) and the file profile\trace.speedscope.json (run profile.sh again if it is missing)
Open https://www.speedscope.app and drag profile\trace.speedscope.json in (it is read locally)
Pick the busiest thread, switch to Sandwich, sort by Self: the SQLite and change-tracking frames are at the top
Terminal next to it: python tools/speedscope_top.py profile/trace.speedscope.json --top 6 --match Reports.MonthlyRevenueAsync
Say on camera that the expected culprit, formatting the date text, is not in the list
mask: Windows user name in the browser file picker and window titles
browser profile picture and bookmarks bar
screens.note: If the laptop has no internet during the recording, use Visual Studio's profiler to open the .nettrace instead (not verified).

screens.name: after
prepare: git apply --check C:\work\01-load-everything.patch 2>$null; if ($?) { git apply C:\work\01-load-everything.patch; dotnet build src/Contoso.Orders.Api -c Release }

if (-not ((Test-Path api.pid) -and (Get-Process -Id (Get-Content api.pid) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue))) { $env:ASPNETCORE_URLS = 'http://localhost:5080'; $env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = 'Production'; $env:Orders__SeedCount = '100000'; $env:ConnectionStrings__Orders = 'Data Source=perf.db'; $api = Start-Process dotnet 'src/Contoso.Orders.Api/bin/Release/net10.0/Contoso.Orders.Api.dll' -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden; $api.Id | Set-Content api.pid; Start-Sleep -Seconds 15 }
screens.note: The first load.py line is the slow build (the script shows 1846 / 2908 ms p50/p95; expect the same order of magnitude), the second the fixed build (20 / 50 ms). Optionally show the red guard message from the patched build: 'one report allocated ... bytes ... the budget is 1,000,000'.

teardown: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='dotnet.exe'" | Where-Object CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api.dll*' | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }
# owner: close the speedscope.app tab (nothing was uploaded)
Set-Location C:\work; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-perf, C:\work\01-load-everything.patch -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
